top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori, Ye) is an invention with a clear original experiment and clean two-name credit. The magic-wavelength lattice cancels the first-order light shift so thousands of atoms can be held in the Lamb-Dicke regime, which is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-system prizes. It is verified directly by clock-to-clock agreement near 1e-18 across independent laboratories and already yields physics such as millimetre-scale redshift.
